explicit_propositions.text: Health care is under attack.
Health care costs increased significantly after the implementation of Obamacare.
Many people lost their health insurance plans after Obamacare was implemented.
People were forced to leave doctors they had previously been allowed to keep.
New health insurance plans available post-Obamacare had extremely high premiums.
Deductibles in new plans became higher after Obamacare.
Prescription drug costs rose after Obamacare.
Copayments increased following Obamacare.
The left is promoting policies based on inflated health care costs.
A comparison of economic records, cost of living, wage growth, and job numbers will be used in the upcoming election.

assumptions.text: The speaker believes that rising health care costs are primarily due to Obamacare.
The speaker trusts personal anecdotes and media narratives over official data regarding health care reform impacts.
The speaker assumes that voters prioritize affordability and continuity of care in health insurance.
The speaker views the political opposition as misrepresenting the effects of health care policy.
The speaker believes that presenting economic comparisons will strengthen their electoral argument.
The speaker considers themselves representative of mainstream voter concerns about health care.
The speaker assumes that 'the left' operates strategically rather than ideologically on health care issues.
The speaker holds that past performance metrics like wages and jobs are valid indicators of policy success.
The speaker expects the public to accept their interpretation of economic trends without requiring detailed evidence.
The speaker believes that emotional appeals around loss of coverage and doctors are effective political tools.
